newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish insurers' profit seen down after flood.
newsitem.headline: Polish insurers' profit seen down after flood.

text.p: Heavy floods which have ravaged southern Poland for nearly three weeks will harm profits of Polish insurance companies, analysts said on Wednesday.
They said insurers' damage payments, estimated so far at 500 million zlotys ($145 million), may reach one billion zlotys.
Non-life insurance is likely to become more popular in the long term because of the floods even though insurers are also likely to increase premiums, they said.

"We can expect that financial results of insurance firms will fall this year... There is information that damages paid by insurers will amount to one billion zloyts," said Robert Sobieraj, insurance analyst at Bank Handlowy's brokerage.
Most analysts warned against forecasting insurers' results before the full scope of damage caused by the flood, which swamped nearly 6,000 square km (2,300 square miles) and killed 55, is known.

"It is difficult to estimate what impact this (flood) will have on financial results...It depends on how premiums are calculated, how risk funds are created," said Artur Szeski of CBM Pekao SA brokerage.
He forecast that Warta will suffer only mild decline in profits. Warta's spokesman Zbigniew Augustynowicz confirmed this.
"The damages will not significantly influence the financial result. We have made sufficient reserves for the damages," Augustynowicz said.

He said that Warta, which had hoped to increase its net profit to between 22 and 25 million zlotys in 1998 from 18.1 million zlotys last year, had deeply reinsured most of assets, now claimed for damages.
Warta estimated its damages at 150-160 million zlotys.
The biggest insurer, the state-owned Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU), earlier said it will have to pay at least 350 million zlotys in damages in two of the 14 affected provinces alone.
Analysts said that Polisa, which estimates its damages at eight million zlotys, will have less trouble from the floodsthan other companies because of its high reinsurance.
Polisa said in a statement it would bear only 20-25 percent of the of damages, with the remainder paid by reinsurers.
